name: Zendesk
description: Tickets, users and organizations in Zendesk Support.

objects.label: tickets
objects.description: Support tickets and the conversation in them.

fields.label: description
fields.description: The first message in the ticket.

fields.label: requester
fields.description: The customer the ticket is for.

fields.label: group
fields.description: The agent group the ticket is routed to.

fields.label: tag
fields.description: Ticket tags, like billing or vip.

objects.label: organizations
objects.description: Companies that end users belong to, usually matched by email domain.

fields.label: tag
fields.description: Organization tags are copied onto new tickets from its users.

actions.label: a ticket
actions.description: One new ticket per record, opened on behalf of the requester.

params.label: for
params.description: The customer the ticket is for. They get the usual ticket emails.

actions.label: a comment on each ticket
actions.description: Reply on the tickets in the source. Public replies go to the requester by email; internal notes stay with agents.

actions.label: a status change
actions.description: Change the status of the tickets in the source. Solved tickets close on their own after a few days; nothing here closes them outright.

guidance: Zendesk is reached through the Support REST API on the company's subdomain (yourcompany.zendesk.com/api/v2) with an API token for an agent account or an OAuth app; every action shows in the ticket audit as that agent, so use a dedicated one. Public comments email the requester immediately, so default to internal notes unless the plan says the customer should see it. Set tickets to Solved at most and never mark them Closed, because closed tickets cannot be reopened or edited.

setup.notes: Ask the Zendesk admin for an agent seat for the automation and an API token from Admin Center. Agent seats are licensed, so raise this early.
